text:
bob_acme: Hey team — our security folks just told me I lost access to Audit Logs in the Console. I used to be able to view them. When I click Compliance -> Audit logs I get a banner: "You do not have permission to view audit logs". We use Okta SSO and groups map to Redwood roles. Org: org_12345, my email bob@acme.com. Can you check?

jess_support: Hi @bob_acme — sorry for the trouble. Quick questions: are you talking about Console read (viewing the audit stream) or exporting historical logs? Also is this the Hosted product?

bob_acme: Just viewing in console, not exporting. Hosted yes. Previously an engineer in our security team could see logs fine; they still can. Only I lost access.

mike_sre: Got it. Historically we gate Console Audit visibility with two things: 1) a read entitlement (audit.read) granted to the org role, and 2) retention/export entitlements for export flows. If another admin can view logs, probably role mapping for your user lost the audit.read entitlement. Do you know which Okta group you’re in (SCIM vs group push)?

bob_acme: We're using Okta SCIM group push. I'm in group "Acme-Sec-Viewers" which used to map to the org role "Org:AuditViewer".

nisha_engineer: Thanks — can you paste the full error banner screenshot or the console request ID? If you press F12 on the console > Network and reload the page, the call is `GET /api/v1/orgs/org_12345/audit/events` and we can look for a 403 with X-Request-Id.

bob_acme: Here's the snippet copied from the console network: ``GET https://console.redwood.ai/api/v1/orgs/org_12345/audit/events 403`` Response headers: ``x-request-id: r-88a2f4ef``.

jess_support: Perfect — I've pulled the request. The API returned 403 because the token linked to your session didn't include the `audit:read` permission. That token is minted by our control plane after SSO assertion mapping. Two likely causes: Okta group attribute changed (stop sending group claim), or our SCIM sync had a failure that removed the entitlement mapping on our side.

mike_sre: Also worth checking SAML/OIDC attributes. For SAML assertions we look for attribute `roles` or `redwood_entitlements`. For OIDC we read `groups` claim or SCIM push. If the IdP changed the attribute name or pattern (e.g., adding a prefix), mapping rules can break.

bob_acme: I asked our IdP team — they say they didn't change anything. They show the SAML assertion includes: ``<saml:Attribute Name="roles">Acme-Sec-Viewers</saml:Attribute>``

nisha_engineer: Ok. Can you also confirm the SCIM group object for Acme-Sec-Viewers still has `externalId: acme-sec-viewers`? We use `externalId` to reconcile groups during push. If that changed, group-to-role mapping can be lost and you'd drop the entitlement.

bob_acme: SCIM shows `externalId` still present.

auditbot: System: SCIM sync failure detected for org_12345 on 1968009000 — delta: group mapping mismatch.

mike_sre: That system message is interesting — looks like we had a transient SCIM error two days ago where group membership events from Okta were rejected (429/500). If the downstream reconciliation job didn't catch up, some users might have stale role state. I'm going to check our SCIM retry queue for group pushes to org_12345.

nisha_engineer: Meanwhile, @jess_support can you ask @olga_pm in the account team to confirm whether the org has a custom entitlement policy? We recently rolled out per-org overrides (e.g., deny-audit for certain partners). I want to rule that out: if an org-level policy denies audit.read, that would override role assignment.

olga_pm: Confirmed: no custom deny policy is on for org_12345. Policies page shows default rules.

mike_sre: I checked the SCIM retry queue and found several failed group-sync events for `Acme-Sec-Viewers` on 1968008502 due to a transient Okta 502. The retry job hasn't reconciled the membership change that re-added your user after a manual change. I'm going to force a reconciliation for org_12345 now.

jess_support: Thanks. @bob_acme — while Mike does that, can you try signing out and back in (full SSO logout) to ensure a fresh session token is minted after reconciliation?

bob_acme: Signed out and back in. Still the same 403.

mike_sre: Forcible reconciliation completed at 1968010000. I also manually re-applied the role mapping: Acme-Sec-Viewers -> Org:AuditViewer (entitlements: audit.read, audit.export-view). I pushed a live policy refresh for the org.

nisha_engineer: On the backend I validated the authz cache for your user (sub:bob@acme.com) — it showed `entitlements: []` before the reconcile and `entitlements: [audit.read, logs.view]` after.

bob_acme: Refreshing console now... got it! I can see the audit stream again. Thank you.

jess_support: Great news — sorry again for the disruption. We should follow up with the IdP team to understand why the SCIM event failed and didn't fully reconcile. Mike, can you open an internal incident to track the SCIM retry edge case so we can add alerts?

mike_sre: Will do. I'll create a short postmortem and add an alert for stuck reconciliation jobs and a retry escalation.

olga_pm: Also looping in account team to let customer know root cause: transient Okta 502 -> SCIM sync failure -> stale role state. We'll offer a short credit for disruption.

bob_acme: Appreciate it — one last question: is there a way for us to self-check entitlements from the console? It would help triage next time.

nisha_engineer: Not yet in the UI, but you can check via API: ``GET /api/v1/orgs/org_12345/members/{user_id}/entitlements`` returns a list of effective entitlements. We're tracking a small UX improvement to surface effective role/entitlement per user in Console. I'll add you as a validation contact for that ticket.

jess_support: Closing this thread since access is restored. If anything else pops up, reopen or ping support with the request-id. :thumbsup:

bob_acme: Thanks everyone!
